name: graykode/abtop
methodology_note: Repo-surface track: this product is distributed as a repository (library/CLI) with no web product surface, so the score derives ONLY from measurable public-repository signals — documentation, licensing, maintenance activity, releases, traction, agent-consumability. Each checklist item carries its evidence. Score ceiling 82/100: VITAL requires hands-on behavioral testing that repo signals cannot provide. Replaces a 2026-06/07 stub that carried a default score with no evidence.

checklist.task: Maintained: pushed within 12 months and not archived
Agent-consumable surface documented (MCP config or CLI install)

summary: graykode/abtop — Like htop, but for AI coding agents. Monitor Claude    Code & Codex CLI sessions, tokens, context window,    rate limits, and ports in real-time.. Repo-surface review: measured from the public repository (3351 stars, MIT, last push 2026-07-07); not hands-on tested.

hlido_opinion.headline: A fast, actively-developed Rust 'htop for AI coding agents' — an excellent human-facing observability tool, not an agent-consumable component.
hlido_opinion.body: This is a healthy young project by every repository signal: MIT-licensed, written in Rust, three CI workflows, tagged releases (v0.5.3) and a push within the last ~9 days. 3.4k stars for a niche tool this young is a strong signal that it scratches a current itch — watching Claude Code and Codex CLI sessions for tokens, context window, rate limits and ports in real time. The honest framing is about audience: this is an operator's TUI, and the repo exposes no agent-consumable surface, so it belongs in the developer's terminal, not in an agent's toolchain. Repo-surface read.

tier_rationale: STEADY (82, repo-surface ceiling). MIT licensing, Rust, multiple CI workflows, an active release cadence and strong early traction clear STEADY. VITAL is withheld because it is early (v0.5.x, API still moving) and, by design, exposes no programmatic surface to verify agent-side.
what_it_does_well: MIT-licensed, Rust performance, and very active (push within ~9 days)
Multiple CI workflows (3) and a steady early release cadence (v0.5.3)
Solves a real, current pain — live visibility into Claude Code / Codex sessions
Strong traction (3.4k stars) for a young, niche tool
what_it_fails_at: No agent-consumable interface — it is a human TUI monitor
Young (v0.5.x) with an API still in motion
Utility is scoped to Claude Code / Codex CLI users
best_for: Developers running Claude Code or Codex who want live session/token/rate-limit visibility

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A human-facing terminal monitor with no programmatic/agent surface. It complements a coding-agent workflow for the operator, but agents cannot drive it. No hands-on behavioral test performed.
